structure:
ruling-design-2026-11-13.md: a short Markdown ruling file, 31 lines, holding design's answers to the three design calls on the "Three Design Calls" page (https://claude.ai/artifact/Ai4JjvLxchDPrPqp39Tj7C), passed on by Sam. Laid out in four pieces, in order: a two-line heading and provenance note (lines 1-4, naming design as the author, Sam as the route and the Three Design Calls page as the question set); a verbatim block quote of design's own words (lines 6-12, four lines: "Ok so I'm going to propose the following", "Include the Add country button", "Implement address searching without live filtering", "People can get a feel for it and if necessary we can return to the area and think of a way to do it", "Don't build the copy buttons"); a "## Decided" section (lines 14-26) with exactly three numbered decisions, each a bolded headline sentence plus the behaviour it keeps, what is not built, and the increment and requirement ids it drops (1. transit countries keep the 'Add country' button, inc-030 dropped with req-348, req-349, req-353, req-354; 2. address search does not filter as the trader types, inc-193 dropped with req-592, req-1951, req-2039; 3. no Copy buttons on the import reference numbers, inc-198 dropped with req-1986); and a closing "Not covered here" paragraph (lines 28-31) naming two areas this ruling does not settle and the earlier rulings that still hold them (inc-194 deferred as concept work under ruling:sam-2026-11-09 point 2, inc-014 commodity search as you type still waiting on its own ticket under ruling:sam-2026-11-10 point 2). The scope is "whole file", so nothing is left out, and the file is far smaller than one part, so it is one part: the whole file read word for word, with the block quote as the source and the three numbered items as the main session's reading to be checked against it.

Extracted in 1 part:
Part 1, The whole 13 November design ruling: Part 1, 'The whole 13 November design ruling': the whole of workareas/shared/design-release-2-1/sources/ruling-design-2026-11-13.md, lines 1-31, read word for word. The file has four pieces, claimed in order. Lines 1-4: the heading 'Ruling: design, 13 November 2026' and a provenance note saying these are design's answers to the three calls on the 'Three Design Calls' page (https://claude.ai/artifact/Ai4JjvLxchDPrPqp39Tj7C), passed on by Sam. Lines 6-12: the verbatim block quote of design's own words, four content lines ('Ok so I'm going to propose the following'; 'Include the Add country button'; 'Implement address searching without live filtering'; 'People can get a feel for it and if necessary we can return to the area and think of a way to do it'; 'Don't build the copy buttons') — this block quote is the source the listed items are checked against. Lines 14-26: '## Decided', three numbered items, each a bolded headline sentence plus the behaviour kept, what is not built, and the increment and requirement ids dropped (1. transit countries keep the 'Add country' button, inc-030 dropped with req-348, req-349, req-353, req-354; 2. address search does not filter as the trader types, inc-193 dropped with req-592, req-1951, req-2039; 3. no Copy buttons on the import reference numbers, inc-198 dropped with req-1986). Lines 28-31: the closing 'Not covered here' paragraph, naming inc-194 (still deferred as concept work under ruling:sam-2026-11-09 point 2) and inc-014 (still waiting on its own ticket under ruling:sam-2026-11-10 point 2). Covered: the provenance and authority; every line of the block quote; all three decisions split into one claim per observable fact (the headline, each behaviour kept, each behaviour not built, each surface it applies to, and the dropped increment and requirement ids); decision 2's open point as a gap rather than a decision; both 'Not covered here' areas recorded as unsettled; and four gaps where the ruling touches something and leaves it open. Each of the three headline sentences is marked verbatim because the block quote says it in so many words; every detail that appears only under '## Decided' (Remove reloading the page, which pickers the search covers, what main already does, which increments and requirements are dropped) is marked inferred, because the block quote names the three calls at headline level only and those details are the main session's reading of it. The file has no earlier extract, so no claim ids are kept.

claims.statement: This ruling carries design's own authority: it is design's answers to the three calls put to it on the 'Three Design Calls' page, and Sam only passed them on.
claims.ref: ruling-design-2026-11-13.md heading and provenance note, lines 1-4
claims.quote:
# Ruling: design, 13 November 2026

Design's answers to the three calls on the "Three Design Calls" page
(https://claude.ai/artifact/Ai4JjvLxchDPrPqp39Tj7C), passed on by Sam.
claims.note: Answers the three design calls set out on the 'Three Design Calls' page (https://claude.ai/artifact/Ai4JjvLxchDPrPqp39Tj7C); the ruling settles those three and nothing else.

claims.statement: Design puts the three answers forward as a proposal in its own words, while the ruling file records them under '## Decided'.
claims.ref: ruling-design-2026-11-13.md block quote, line 6, read against the '## Decided' heading at line 14
claims.quote: Ok so I'm going to propose the following
claims.note: Recorded as an ambiguity, not resolved: design's word is 'propose', the file's heading is 'Decided'. The main session wrote the file and treats all three as decided.

claims.statement: Transit countries keep the 'Add country' button.
claims.ref: ruling-design-2026-11-13.md block quote line 8, and '## Decided' item 1 headline, line 16
claims.quote: Include the Add country button
claims.note: The Decided item's headline says the same thing in the file's own words: "**Transit countries keep the 'Add country' button.**".

claims.statement: Address searching is built without live filtering: the search does not filter as the trader types.
claims.ref: ruling-design-2026-11-13.md block quote line 9, and '## Decided' item 2 headline, line 20
claims.quote: Implement address searching without live filtering
claims.note: The Decided item's headline says the same thing in the file's own words: '**Address search does not filter as the trader types.**'.

claims.statement: Design expects people to use the address search without live filtering first, and may return to the area afterwards to think of a way to do the filtering.
claims.quote: People can get a feel for it and if necessary we can return to the area and think of a way to do it
claims.note: A possibility design holds open, not a decision to build anything: 'if necessary'. See the gap claim ruling-design-2026-11-13-p1-022 for what it leaves open.

claims.statement: The copy buttons are not built.
claims.ref: ruling-design-2026-11-13.md block quote line 12, and '## Decided' item 3 headline, line 24
claims.quote: Don't build the copy buttons
claims.note: The Decided item's headline names where they would have gone, in the file's own words: '**No Copy buttons on the import reference numbers.**'.

claims.statement: A transit country is added to the list only when the trader presses 'Add country', and not as soon as the country is picked.
claims.quote:
A country is added when the trader presses 'Add country',
   not as soon as it is picked
claims.note: Design's own words are only 'Include the Add country button'; the two-step add follows from keeping the button, and this sentence is the main session's reading of it.

claims.statement: Removing a transit country reloads the page.
claims.quote: and Remove reloads the page
claims.note: Design's block quote says nothing about Remove; this detail is the main session's reading, consistent with keeping the button-driven, no-JavaScript pattern.

claims.statement: The transit-countries add-and-remove behaviour the ruling keeps is what main already does, so nothing has to change there.
claims.quote: This is what main already does.
claims.note: The block quote does not mention main; the main session added the observation that the kept behaviour is already built.

claims.statement: Adding a transit country as soon as it is picked is not built.
claims.quote:
Adding on pick,
   removing in place and the 'Added' and 'Removed' announcements are not built
claims.note: Follows from design's 'Include the Add country button'; the explicit not-built list is the main session's reading.

claims.statement: Removing a transit country in place, without reloading the page, is not built.
claims.quote:
Adding on pick,
   removing in place and the 'Added' and 'Removed' announcements are not built
claims.note: Not in design's own words; the main session's reading of keeping the button.

claims.statement: The 'Added' and 'Removed' announcements on the transit countries list are not built.
claims.quote:
Adding on pick,
   removing in place and the 'Added' and 'Removed' announcements are not built
claims.note: Not in design's own words; the main session's reading of keeping the button.

claims.statement: Increment inc-030 is dropped, and requirements req-348, req-349, req-353 and req-354 are out of scope.
claims.quote:
(inc-030 dropped: req-348, req-349,
   req-353, req-354 out of scope)
claims.note: The increment and requirement ids are the main session's mapping of design's decision onto the backlog, not design's own words.

claims.statement: To search for an address the trader types a term and then presses Search or Enter.
claims.quote: The trader types, then presses Search or Enter
claims.note: Design's own words are 'Implement address searching without live filtering'; the type-then-submit interaction, including Enter as well as the Search button, is the main session's reading.

claims.statement: The non-filtering address search applies on every party picker.
claims.quote:
on every
   party picker, the place of origin picker and the address book list
claims.note: Design's block quote names no surfaces; the three places are the main session's reading.

claims.statement: The non-filtering address search applies on the place of origin picker.
claims.quote:
on every
   party picker, the place of origin picker and the address book list
claims.note: Design's block quote names no surfaces; the three places are the main session's reading.

claims.statement: The non-filtering address search applies on the address book list.
claims.quote:
on every
   party picker, the place of origin picker and the address book list
claims.note: Design's block quote names no surfaces; the three places are the main session's reading.

claims.statement: The address search kept by the ruling is the server-side search main already has, so nothing has to change there.
claims.quote:
This is the server search main already
   has.
claims.note: The block quote does not mention main or server-side searching; the main session added the observation that the kept behaviour is already built.

claims.statement: Address rows that filter as the trader types are not built.
claims.quote: The rows that filter as the trader types are not built
claims.note: Follows directly from design's 'without live filtering'; the wording about rows is the main session's reading.

claims.statement: Increment inc-193 is dropped, and requirements req-592, req-1951 and req-2039 are out of scope.
claims.quote:
(inc-193 dropped: req-592, req-1951, req-2039 out
   of scope)
claims.note: The increment and requirement ids are the main session's mapping of design's decision onto the backlog, not design's own words.

claims.statement: If design comes back to address-search filtering after people have used the service, it re-enters as a new question rather than as part of this ruling.
claims.quote: Design may come back to this area once people have used it; if so, it returns as a new question.
claims.note: Design's own words are 'if necessary we can return to the area and think of a way to do it'; that it would return as a new question is the main session's reading. Not a decision to build anything now.

claims.statement: The ruling leaves open whether address search will ever filter as the trader types, and says nothing about what would trigger the return to the area, who decides, what evidence from people using it would count, or what the filtering design would be.
claims.ref: ruling-design-2026-11-13.md block quote line 10 and '## Decided' item 2, line 23
claims.note: Recorded as an open point, not a decision: design only says 'if necessary we can return to the area and think of a way to do it'. Nothing is to be built for it now.

claims.statement: The import reference number stays as text the trader can select, with no Copy button.
claims.quote:
The reference and customs code stay as text the trader
   can select
claims.note: Design's own words are only "Don't build the copy buttons"; that the reference stays as selectable text is the main session's reading.

claims.statement: The customs code stays as text the trader can select, with no Copy button.
claims.quote:
The reference and customs code stay as text the trader
   can select
claims.note: Design's own words are only "Don't build the copy buttons"; that the customs code stays as selectable text is the main session's reading.

claims.statement: The reference and customs code are already built as selectable text in the overview-and-review header row, so nothing has to change there.
claims.quote: as the overview-and-review header row already builds them
claims.note: The block quote does not mention the overview-and-review header row; the main session added where the kept behaviour already lives.

claims.statement: Increment inc-198 is dropped, and requirement req-1986 is out of scope.
claims.quote:
(inc-198 dropped: req-1986 out of
   scope)
claims.note: The increment and requirement ids are the main session's mapping of design's decision onto the backlog, not design's own words.

claims.statement: This ruling does not settle address search's search-only layout or its lookup results as you type (inc-194): those stay deferred as concept work under ruling:sam-2026-11-09 point 2.
claims.quote:
Not covered here: address search's search-only layout and lookup results as you type (inc-194) stay deferred as
concept work under ruling:sam-2026-11-09 point 2.
claims.note: Recorded as an area this ruling leaves to an earlier ruling, not as a decision of this file. Its decision 2 (no filtering as the trader types) and inc-194 both touch address search, so the two must not be read as the same point.

claims.statement: This ruling does not settle commodity search as you type (inc-014): it still waits on its own ticket under ruling:sam-2026-11-10 point 2.
claims.quote:
Commodity search as you type (inc-014) still waits on its own
ticket under ruling:sam-2026-11-10 point 2.
claims.note: Recorded as an area this ruling leaves to an earlier ruling, not as a decision of this file. Decision 2 is about address search only and does not decide commodity search.

claims.statement: The ruling says nothing about whether the high-risk plants frontend mirrors these three decisions, even though the pages they touch (party and place-of-origin pickers, the transit-countries list, reference numbers) exist there too.
claims.note: The programme's goal makes a plants mirror part of each shared row; this ruling is silent on it, so the silence is recorded rather than read either way.

claims.statement: The ruling settles the add-then-press pattern for transit countries only, and does not say whether other add-another collections follow the same two-step add and page-reload Remove.
claims.note: Design's words, 'Include the Add country button', name the country case alone, so the wider pattern is left open.

claims.statement: The ruling names only the overview-and-review header row, and does not say whether reference numbers shown anywhere else also stay as plain selectable text with no Copy button.
claims.note: 'Don't build the copy buttons' is unqualified in design's words, while the Decided item cites one surface; what holds on any other surface showing a reference is left open.
